title: Reliable Multi-Agent Handoffs
summary: This intermediate module enables learners to design a clear handoff between agents, evaluate whether the receiving agent accepted it, and recover when required information is missing. After completing it, learners can turn an informal transfer of work into a reviewable handoff contract.
objectives: Create a handoff contract that identifies the task, relevant context, constraints, expected output, and success criteria.
Check whether a receiving agent has accepted a handoff and has enough information to proceed.
Recognize an incomplete or ambiguous handoff and select an appropriate recovery action.
Separate information needed for the next task from unrelated conversation history.

sections.title: Level and scope
paragraphs: This is an intermediate-level module. It assumes that you understand the basic idea of an agent as a software role that receives information, performs a task, and produces a result. No knowledge of a particular provider, product, programming language, or configuration format is required.

A multi-agent workflow divides work among multiple roles. Communication between those roles is part of the workflow design described in the cited survey. This module focuses on one communication event: transferring responsibility for a task from one agent to another.

sections.title: What changed in this update
paragraphs: The previous citation, content/modules/reliable-agent-workflows/multi-agent-handoffs.json, changed because it was an unverified repository path rather than a reader-resolvable HTTPS source. It has been replaced by the canonical arXiv record for A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents.

This correction affects the source record and the evidentiary boundary of the module. Claims attributed only to the previous unverified path are UNKNOWN and are omitted. The revised material remains provider-neutral and does not introduce tool-specific instructions, version requirements, or configuration keys.
sections.callout: The source correction supports the general discussion of communication among agents. The handoff contract below is a teaching framework used by this module, not a claim that every multi-agent system uses one mandatory format.

sections.title: Build a handoff contract
paragraphs: For this module, a handoff contract is the information the sending agent provides so that the receiving agent can understand the assigned work and determine whether it can proceed. Use five parts: the task, relevant context, constraints, expected output, and success criteria.

The task states what the receiving agent is responsible for doing. Relevant context includes only information needed to perform that task. Constraints state boundaries the receiver must respect. The expected output describes what the receiver should return. Success criteria explain how the result will be judged.

A handoff should be specific enough to review. For example, replace a vague task such as continue the work with a concrete task such as review the supplied draft for unsupported factual claims. The second form identifies an action and gives the receiving agent a basis for reporting completion.

sections.title: Confirm acceptance and validate the result
paragraphs: A sent handoff is not automatically an accepted handoff. The receiving agent should indicate whether it understands the task, has the required context, and can follow the constraints. If any required element is missing or contradictory, the receiver should request clarification rather than silently inventing an answer.

After the receiver returns a result, compare that result with the expected output and success criteria in the handoff contract. A fluent response is not enough by itself. The result must address the assigned task and respect the stated constraints.
Keep the acceptance check distinct from the final result check. Acceptance asks whether the receiver can begin responsibly. Validation asks whether the completed result satisfies the contract.

sections.title: Recover from a failed handoff
paragraphs: When a handoff is incomplete, first identify the missing or conflicting element. Ask for the smallest clarification that resolves the problem, then issue a corrected handoff and seek acceptance again.

When the receiving agent cannot perform the task under the stated constraints, do not treat that response as successful completion. Return responsibility to the sending role, revise the task or constraints, or choose a different receiving role.

Preserve enough of the handoff and response to explain what was requested, what was accepted, and why a correction occurred. Avoid transferring unrelated conversation history when a concise statement of relevant context is sufficient.

questions.prompt: Which option contains all five parts of the handoff contract taught in this module?
choices: Task, relevant context, constraints, expected output, and success criteria
Task, full conversation history, provider name, version number, and success criteria
Agent name, task, product key, retry count, and expected output
Relevant context, informal suggestion, tool version, hidden reasoning, and deadline
questions.explanation: The module defines its handoff contract using the task, relevant context, constraints, expected output, and success criteria.

questions.prompt: What should happen when the receiving agent finds that required context is missing?
choices: It should invent the missing context and continue.
It should request clarification before proceeding.
It should report successful completion immediately.
It should ignore the handoff constraints.
questions.explanation: The acceptance process requires the receiver to request clarification when a required element is missing or contradictory.

questions.prompt: How should a returned result be validated?
choices: Check only whether the response is fluent.
Check whether the receiving agent used a particular provider.
Compare the result with the expected output and success criteria.
Accept every result once the handoff has been sent.
questions.explanation: The module instructs the learner to compare the returned result with the contract's expected output and success criteria.

questions.prompt: What did the cited-source correction affect?
choices: It changed the module to a provider-specific lesson.
It affected the source record and the module's evidentiary boundary.
It established that every system uses one mandatory handoff format.
questions.explanation: The update replaces an unverified repository path with a canonical HTTPS source and omits claims that depended only on the previous path.
